items.t: Streaming premieres: New Korean series ‘Dead-End Job’; Liev Schreiber in Apple TV’s ‘Nocturne’
items.x: Streaming Friday, Oct. 30: Dead-End Job — The promise of hourly pay that’s 50 times the minimum wage puts a cash-strapped Korean behind the counter of a convenience store where every shift is like a contest on Squid Game.

items.t: Orlando music community pays homage with Dolly Parton tribute
items.x: Orlando musicians gathering for the Dolly Parton tribute include Rachel Decker, Sarah Rogo, Amy Robbins, Jordan Schneider, Rickey Dickens, David Minshew & Michael Rizzo, Edan Archer and Devin & Gage, among others.

items.t: An oral history of pioneering Orlando attraction Terror on Church Street
items.x: Take a look back at a legendary Orlando haunted attraction that set and set a standard for screams that still echoes throughout the industry today, decades after it disappeared.

items.t: Orange County has erased more than $750M in medical debt, exceeding expectations
items.x: Orange County announced Tuesday that it has exceeded its expectations for a medical debt relief initiative that the county first kicked off in 2024.

items.x: State Attorney Monique Worrell announced the conviction last week, emphasizing that the diamond theft also put Tiffany store employees at risk.

items.x: An Orlandoan twist on the French doner kebab now appears on the menu of Albatross, a new collab concept by Giovanny Artiga, Eliot Hillis and Seth Parker.

items.t: Sand cliffs up to 14 feet high damage Brevard County coastline
items.x: Strong winds and high tides caused major beach erosion in Brevard County, creating sand cliffs up to 14 feet high.

items.t: Woman dies after being thrown ﻿from motorcycle on Florida highway
items.x: A 19-year-old woman is dead after she was thrown from the motorcycle she was a passenger on and hit by a semi-truck on I-95 in Ormond Beach.

items.t: How many alligators are in Florida? The state once counted
items.x: The conventional wisdom in Florida is that if you see a body of water, assume there is a gator in it. But some bodies of water have more than others — quite a few more.

items.t: Strike on Darfur market killed civilians selling food to fighters, witnesses say
items.x: Witnesses in Sudan say that multiple civilian vendors are among the dozens reportedly killed in an attack on a market earlier this week in a poverty-stricken Darfur city in southwestern Sudan.

items.t: Georgia's Keisha Lance Bottoms navigates the challenges of Black women battling political barriers
items.x: Georgia Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms is trying to make history as the first woman to be elected governor in the United States.

items.t: Three men arrested after haircut stunt in Ocala leaves teenager seriously injured
items.x: Ocala police arrested three youths following a dangerous social media challenge on State Road 200 that left one injured.

items.t: Justin Tucker joining the Chiefs' practice squad after 10-game suspension last year, AP source says
items.x: The Kansas City Chiefs are signing Justin Tucker to their practice squad, according to a person familiar with the move.

items.t: Officer accused of using deceased man’s identity to acquire home resigns from force
items.x: The City of Lauderhill announced that police officer Brian Sguros had resigned his position. The former officer is facing five charges, including identity theft.

items.t: Spain train crash: Death toll rises
items.x: A high-speed train collision in Toledo, Spain, left at least 30 dead and disrupted rail service to Andalusia.

items.t: Daytona Beach commissioners to discuss fencing around retention ponds
items.x: After two young brothers drowned in a Daytona Beach retention pond earlier this month, city commissioners are set to discuss whether more ponds should be fenced.
